Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Peachtree City GA
650 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

...New 12Z Aviation Discussion...

.KEY MESSAGES...

 - Scattered to numerous showers and storms expected each day 
   through the weekend. 

 - Heavy rainfall may lead to isolated instances of flash 
   flooding across North and Central Georgia today and Friday. 

 - Seasonable temperatures are largely expected through early 
   next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Friday)
Issued at 314 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Currently: A few spotty showers have already begun to pop up across 
the area this morning per latest radar imagery. Though the main 
action is well to our west across the ArkLaMiss where a storm 
complex is pushing southward. High cirrus from this complex is 
beginning to blanket across the area with low to mid-level clouds 
starting to fill in underneath. Isolated showers and perhaps a 
rumble of thunder will be possible through the morning and is not 
expected to come from the storm complex to our west. 

Storm Chances and Flood Potential: Increased coverage of showers and 
storms as well as a potential for locally heavy rainfall and 
isolated instances of flash flooding is anticipated for today into 
Friday. A weak frontal boundary over Central GA (roughly LaGrange to 
south of Athens) will be the initial focus area for storm 
development later today. The most notable change from previous 
forecasts is a shift in the area of highest moisture -- reflected in 
the latest PW analysis and HREF 6-hr QPF PMM. Likely a result of 
storm complex to our southwest. While the signal for heavy rainfall 
and flash flooding is not quite as strong for today, high moisture 
content in the atmosphere (PWs 1.5-1.8") means storms will still be 
efficient rain-producers. This coupled with limited shear means 
storms may still present a localized flash flood threat due to heavy 
rainfall in a short period or due to storms repeatedly moving over 
the same areas. Exactly where these storms set up is the biggest 
question but I suspect it will be in the vicinity of the frontal 
boundary draped over the area. Coverage of showers and storms should 
begin decreasing after sunset but isolated shower and storms could 
continue overnight. A vort max will usher another front towards the 
forecast area tonight and it will likely stall just north of the 
area. Ample moisture south of this boundary and temperatures warming 
into the mid to upper 80s on Friday may support pockets of moderate 
instability across North GA. While shear will be fairly weak, if any 
storms are able to take advantage of the flow aloft, they could be 
capable of producing strong to damaging wind gusts. This threat is 
highlighted by a Marginal Risk (Level 1 of 5) by SPC for Friday 
across parts of North GA. 

Temperature Trends: Seasonable temperatures are largely expected for 
today and Friday. Higher cloud cover both days will result in 
daytime highs in the 80s to low 90s. Morning lows are forecast to be 
in the upper 60s to low 70s (slightly cooler in the mountains).

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Friday night through Wednesday)
Issued at 314 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Rather unsurprising, the upper level pattern going into the long 
term outlook (beginning Sat) is dependent on the speed at which the 
eastern CONUS trough exits the area. Ensemble analysis shows the 
majority (68%) of members from GEFS and ENS move the trough out on 
Saturday, with only 6-12% holding the trough into Late 
Saturday/early Sunday. What this means is one last enhanced day for 
upper level enhancement of precip, before the ridge moves overhead. 
Given PWATs over 2" and slow moving/greater coverage of storms, 
excessive rainfall is possible into Saturday. This will be 
especially true for areas which see heavy rain in days prior.

As the ridge moves overhear, conditions will transition more to a 
typical summertime pattern with highs in the 90s and heat indices 
back in the triple digits. While afternoon thunderstorms coverage 
won't be nearly as high, we will likely see disorganized diurnal 
convection each afternoon through next week. As is common with 
summertime convection, a few storms could become strong to even 
severe each afternoon with gusty winds, frequent lightning, and 
locally heavy rainfall. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 634 AM EDT Thu Aug 27 2026

A mixed bag of clouds this morning with high cirrus and low to 
midlevel clouds filling in underneath. Patchy IFR to MVFR cigs and
BR psbl again between 09-14z mainly for MCN and AHN, followed by 
mostly VFR thru the afternoon. Light, vrb wind overnight picking 
up from the SE to SW 3-6kts by around 14z. Sct shra and Iso tsra
already ongoing west and north of the ATL sites and CSG with
coverage expected to increase through the day. Coverage should 
largely dissipate after 00z but iso activity could linger thru 
the night.

//ATL Confidence...12Z Update...

Medium to high confidence on all elements.

07

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
Athens          91  70  89  69 /  30  50  50  40 
Atlanta         90  72  89  71 /  50  30  50  30 
Blairsville     85  64  84  62 /  60  30  50  10 
Cartersville    91  70  90  68 /  40  20  40  20 
Columbus        92  73  90  72 /  70  50  70  30 
Gainesville     89  70  88  68 /  40  40  50  30 
Macon           91  71  88  71 /  60  50  60  40 
Rome            91  69  90  67 /  30  30  40  10 
Peachtree City  90  70  89  68 /  60  40  50  30 
Vidalia         92  72  90  72 /  60  40  60  60 

&&

.FFC WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...07
LONG TERM....SM
AVIATION...07
